documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

28F here to establish care. Previously seen at a primary care office out of the area; she moved to Westhampton and wanted someone local. Records release signed today.

HPI / background
- Hepatitis C: picked up on routine screening in 2015 at her old practice. Told it was "chronic" and she would need a liver doctor, but she never got to the referral and has never been treated. No jaundice, no itching, no abdominal swelling, no GI bleeding that she knows of. Has not had a liver scan that she remembers.
- Substance use: used IV drugs in her early twenties, stopped in 2014 and has not used since. Never on buprenorphine or methadone. Says she does not feel at risk of returning to use; has a stable job and routine. No current alcohol.
- Feels well otherwise. No chronic meds.

PMH: chronic hepatitis C; IV drug use, in sustained remission since 2014
PSH: none
Meds: none
Allergies: NKDA
FHx: mother with type 2 diabetes; paternal grandmother had breast cancer
SHx: administrative coordinator. Former smoker, quit 2014 along with everything else. No alcohol. Single. Medicaid.
GYN: periods regular. Last Pap 2018 at prior office, she was told normal.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam
Gen: well appearing, NAD
HEENT: sclerae anicteric, oropharynx clear
Neck: supple, no thyromegaly, no adenopathy
CV: RRR, no murmur
Lungs: clear bilaterally
Abd: soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly, no ascites
Skin: no jaundice, no spider angiomata, no palmar erythema
Ext: no edema
Psych: normal mood and affect

Assessment / Plan
1. Chronic hepatitis C, never treated. CMP and CBC today for baseline. Referral placed to hepatology to discuss staging and treatment; she is interested now. Avoid alcohol.
2. History of IV drug use in sustained remission. Supportive, nothing needed today.
3. Health maintenance: HIV screen today. Will get Pap result from prior office; due again 2021 or with cotest later. Flu shot when available next month.
4. PHQ-9 = 2.

RTC 1 year or sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Caitlin, your labs from Tuesday are in. Your liver tests (ALT and AST) are mildly above the normal range, which is what we expect with hepatitis C and is not alarming. Bilirubin, albumin, kidney function and platelets are normal, and your blood count is fine. Your HIV test was negative. Hepatology should be calling you to set up the visit; let us know if you haven't heard from them in two weeks.

reports.text: Specimen adequate for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Hepatology consultation
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
HEPATOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 11/19/2019
Referred by: primary care

Dear colleague,

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Maguire, a 28-year-old woman with chronic hepatitis C infection identified on screening in 2015 and never treated. Her presumed exposure is prior injection drug use, which she stopped in 2014. She feels well. She denies jaundice, pruritus, confusion, abdominal distension, melena or hematemesis. No alcohol.

Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Medications: none.

Exam: alert, anicteric. No stigmata of chronic liver disease. Abdomen soft, no palpable liver edge or spleen tip, no ascites.

Liver stiffness by transient elastography today: 5.8 kPa, consistent with no significant fibrosis (F0-F1).

Impression: chronic hepatitis C without significant fibrosis. She is a good candidate for direct-acting antiviral therapy.

Plan:
- Sofosbuvir-velpatasvir daily for 12 weeks once Medicaid prior authorization is approved; our office will submit.
- Urine pregnancy test the day she picks up the first fill, as she is of childbearing age.
- Continue to avoid alcohol.
- We will see her at week 4 of treatment.

Allergies reviewed: NKDA.

Sincerely,
Hepatology

documents.title: Hep C medicine
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
Hi, the liver office said they sent the insurance paperwork for the hep C pills. Do you need to do anything on your end? I haven't heard anything in 2 weeks.

Reply (MA, 12/11): Hi Caitlin, the prior authorization is handled by the hepatology office since they wrote the prescription. I called them this morning and they said it is still with Medicaid and they expect an answer by the end of the month. They will call you directly.

documents.title: Positive home pregnancy test
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt called. Positive home pregnancy test this morning, first day of LMP was 12/7/19. No bleeding, no cramping. She has not started the hepatitis C medication yet; hepatology's prior auth was approved last week and she was due to pick it up Friday.

Advised: do NOT start the hep C medication. Start prenatal vitamin daily. Reviewed with PCP, who agrees; PNV sent to her pharmacy. Called hepatology nurse line and left message re: pregnancy and hold on treatment.

She would like to go to the OB group in town. Referral placed. Pt verbalized understanding.

Addendum 1/9 RN: hepatology nurse called back. Treatment on hold until after delivery. They will reach out to her postpartum.

Patient informed us of a new pregnancy before her first fill. Sofosbuvir-velpatasvir will not be started. The approved authorization will lapse; we will resubmit when she is ready after delivery and breastfeeding. Please have her contact us postpartum. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — LABOR & DELIVERY
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 07/18/2020   Discharged: 08/03/2020
Attending service: Obstetrics

Admission diagnosis: preterm premature rupture of membranes at 32w0d.
Discharge diagnosis: same; delivered at 34w0d.

History: 29-year-old G1 with chronic hepatitis C and remote injection drug use, now in remission, presented with two hours of leaking clear fluid. No contractions, no bleeding, no intercourse recently. Prenatal care has been regular and the pregnancy otherwise uncomplicated.

On arrival: BP 120/75, pulse 80, respirations 16, temperature 37.0 C (98.6 F). Sterile speculum exam: clear fluid pooled in the posterior fornix; nitrazine positive; ferning on microscopy. Fetal monitoring reassuring — baseline 140, moderate variability, no decelerations; no contractions on toco.
Labs: hemoglobin 12.5, WBC 9,000, platelets 250,000. CRP normal.

Hospital course: admitted for expectant management. Betamethasone 12 mg IM given, two doses 24 hours apart. Latency antibiotics for 7 days: IV ampicillin and erythromycin for 48 hours, then oral amoxicillin and erythromycin. She remained afebrile with reassuring fetal testing throughout. Induction at 34w0d on 08/01/2020, uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Liveborn infant admitted to the special care nursery for prematurity. Postpartum course routine.

Tdap given in clinic 06/22/2020.

Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: postpartum visit with OB in 6 weeks; primary care in 2 weeks; hepatology after delivery to revisit treatment.

documents.title: Patient admitted
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called from the hospital to let us know she was admitted Saturday at 32 weeks with her water breaking. Getting steroids and antibiotics, plan is to keep her pregnant to 34 weeks if possible. Asked that we get the records. Will watch for discharge summary; PCP informed.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transition call after hospital discharge 8/3. Discharge summary in chart. She is home, feels well, bleeding moderate and decreasing, no fever, pain controlled with nothing stronger than OTC. Baby still in special care nursery, she is pumping and visiting daily. Taking PNV. Scheduled with PCP 8/18 at 2 pm.

documents.title: Post-discharge follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 29F, 2.5 weeks postpartum. Admitted 7/18 at 32 weeks with ruptured membranes; got steroids and antibiotics, induced at 34 weeks, vaginal delivery 8/1. Discharge summary reviewed. Baby was in the special care nursery for about a week and is home now and feeding well. She is breastfeeding.
Bleeding tapering, lochia light. No fever. Mild perineal soreness. Sleeping in pieces but mood is good. Still on prenatal vitamin.
Hep C: hepatology told her they'd revisit treatment after delivery. She wants to breastfeed for a while first and is asking whether she has to start right away.

O: well appearing. Abd soft, fundus not palpable above the pubis. Calves soft, nontender. Mood and affect normal.

A/P:
1. Postpartum after PPROM and preterm delivery at 34 weeks — recovering as expected. OB postpartum visit already booked for mid-September.
2. Chronic hepatitis C — explained treatment is usually deferred while breastfeeding; she'll call hepatology to arrange a follow-up visit this winter.
3. PHQ-9 3. Reviewed warning signs of postpartum depression; she knows to call.
4. Flu shot this fall.

documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
HEPATOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 03/16/2021

Ms. Maguire returns about seven months after delivering at 34 weeks. Treatment for her chronic hepatitis C was put on hold in January 2020 when she became pregnant. She is still breastfeeding and would prefer not to take any new medication until she has weaned. She feels well, with no jaundice or itching.

Meds: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: anicteric, abdomen benign, no stigmata of chronic liver disease.

Assessment: chronic hepatitis C with no significant fibrosis on elastography in 11/2019 (5.8 kPa). Low short-term risk; deferral is reasonable.

Plan: she will call us when she has finished breastfeeding and is not pregnant, and we will resubmit for sofosbuvir-velpatasvir 12 weeks. No alcohol.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in her care.
Hepatology

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — OBSTETRICS
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission: 07/24/2022   Discharge: 07/30/2022
Admitting diagnosis: pruritus with abnormal liver tests at 35w0d
Principal diagnosis: acute fatty liver of pregnancy
Secondary: chronic hepatitis C; history of PPROM with preterm delivery (2020); hepatitis B non-immune

HPI: 31-year-old G2P0101 sent in from the OB office after two weeks of intense itching, mostly of the palms and soles and worse overnight. No rash, no yellowing, no nausea or vomiting, no change in stools. She had no prior problems this pregnancy.
Exam on arrival: no excoriations or rash. Fundal height appropriate for dates. Fetal heart tones normal.

Initial labs: total bile acids 45 umol/L; ALT 70, AST 68, alkaline phosphatase 120, total bilirubin 1.2.

Course: repeat labs early the next morning showed glucose 58, uric acid 7.9, WBC 14.8, PT 16.2 seconds with INR 1.5. RUQ ultrasound showed a diffusely echogenic liver without biliary dilation. With these findings the diagnosis of acute fatty liver of pregnancy was made. She was transferred to the ICU for monitoring, started on a dextrose infusion, and induced. Uncomplicated vaginal delivery 07/25/2022 at 35w1d; liveborn infant to the nursery. Glucose stabilized within 24 hours of delivery, coagulation studies and transaminases improved daily, and she returned to the postpartum floor on day 2. Itching resolved after delivery.

Tdap given at the OB office 06/06/2022.

Discharge meds: prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 2 weeks for repeat CMP, CBC and PT/INR; OB postpartum visit at 6 weeks.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transition call. Discharge summary from OB admission received yesterday (acute fatty liver of pregnancy, delivered 7/25). She is home with the baby, feels tired but OK. Itching is gone. Eating normally. No confusion, no yellow eyes, no bleeding beyond expected lochia. Booked with PCP 8/9 with labs same day.

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective
31 y/o, 2 weeks postpartum. Admitted 7/24 at 35 weeks for itching with abnormal LFTs; next morning low sugar, high uric acid, prolonged PT and an echogenic liver on US, diagnosed with acute fatty liver of pregnancy, monitored in ICU, induced and delivered vaginally 7/25. I reviewed the discharge summary in full.
Today: itching completely gone since delivery. Appetite good. No RUQ pain, no confusion, no easy bruising. Lochia light. Formula feeding this time. Baby well.
Meds: prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Objective
Vitals reviewed. Well appearing, anicteric. Abd soft, nontender, no HSM. No asterixis. Skin without bruising.

Assessment and plan
1. Acute fatty liver of pregnancy, resolved clinically. Repeat CMP, CBC w/ diff, PT/INR today. Expect enzymes back to her usual mild hep C elevation.
2. Chronic hep C. Not breastfeeding this time — good window to treat. She says she wants to "get settled" first and will think about calling hepatology in the fall. Encouraged her not to let it slide.
3. Mood: PHQ-9 4, tired more than down. Knows to reach out.
4. Flu and updated COVID vaccine in October.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news — your blood sugar, clotting test (INR) and blood counts are normal again, and your liver enzymes are back to where they usually run with hepatitis C. Nothing else to repeat for the fatty liver of pregnancy.

32 y/o here for yearly physical. Two children at home (almost 3 and 10 months). Working, busy, no new concerns.

Hep C: we talked about it again. She knows treatment is 12 weeks of pills and that nothing has changed on her side. Still not ready — wants to wait until "things calm down." I gave her the hepatology number again and offered to re-send the referral whenever she wants; she will message me.

Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vaginal mucosa and cervix normal; Pap/HPV collected. Skin clear. No edema. Mood and affect appropriate.

Plan
- Pap with HPV cotest today.
- CMP, CBC.
- PHQ-9 2.
- Flu and updated COVID vaccine in the fall.
- Hep C: patient deferring; revisit next visit.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL — LABOR AND DELIVERY / OBSTETRIC ICU
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 07/20/2024   Discharged 07/24/2024
Principal diagnosis: placental abruption at 34w0d
Other diagnoses: severe polyhydramnios this pregnancy; chronic hepatitis C; prior PPROM (2020) and acute fatty liver of pregnancy (2022); hepatitis B non-immune
Procedure: emergency low transverse cesarean delivery 07/20/2024

Presentation: 33-year-old G3P0202 at 34 weeks with abrupt onset of sharp, constant lower abdominal pain, 8/10, and vaginal bleeding. No trauma, no recent intercourse. This pregnancy had been followed for severe polyhydramnios.
On arrival BP 140/90, HR 110. Uterus tender with frequent contractions. Fetal monitoring with repetitive late decelerations.
Labs: Hgb 10.2 (baseline 12.5), platelets 210K, PT 12 s, aPTT 30 s, fibrinogen 400.

Course: clinical placental abruption with a non-reassuring tracing. Taken for emergency cesarean the same afternoon. Liveborn infant to the NICU. She was observed in the obstetric ICU overnight, then transferred to postpartum. Hemodynamically stable thereafter; incision clean. Ambulating, tolerating diet.

Tdap given 06/10/2024 at the OB office.

Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin daily; ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed; acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed. No opioid prescribed at discharge in view of her history; patient agreed.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Follow-up: incision check with OB in 1-2 weeks; postpartum visit at 6 weeks; PCP in 2 weeks.

33F seen 2.5 weeks after emergency C-section for placental abruption at 34 weeks (7/20). Discharge summary reviewed: presented with sudden pain and bleeding, BP 140/90, HR 110, late decels, Hgb 10.2 with normal coags; cesarean same day; baby in NICU, home now. This pregnancy also had severe polyhydramnios.

She is sore but improving, off ibuprofen most days. Incision check with OB last week was fine. Bleeding light. No fever, no calf pain, no chest pain or shortness of breath. Tired. Three kids at home now.

Exam: BP and pulse normal today. Afebrile. Low transverse incision clean, dry, well approximated, no erythema. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near incision. Calves soft. Mood a little flat but appropriate, good eye contact.

A/P
1. s/p emergency cesarean for abruption — healing well. CBC today.
2. PHQ-9 5 — mild, mostly sleep and fatigue; no SI. Recheck at next contact; OB will also screen at 6 weeks.
3. Chronic hep C — not raised today; she has enough going on.
4. Flu/COVID in October; can recheck CBC then.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Preventive visit — 34F

Interval: c-section for abruption 7/2024; recovered well, Hgb normal by October. Kids healthy. Working full time as an administrative coordinator.

Hep C — raised again. Still prefers to wait; says she'll "do it when life slows down." Discussed that the scan in 2019 showed no scarring and her labs have been steady, but untreated infection does slowly harm the liver over years and treatment is short and very effective. She heard me; not ready. Will message when she is.
Sustained remission, 11 years. No tobacco since 2014. No alcohol.

Medications: prenatal vitamin daily
Allergies: NKDA

ROS negative.

Exam
Well appearing. Anicteric. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender; healed low transverse scar; no hepatosplenomegaly. No edema. Skin: no jaundice or spider angiomata. Affect normal.

Assessment/Plan
- Adult preventive: PHQ-9 2. Pap/HPV 2023 normal, next 2028. Flu and COVID each fall.
- Chronic hepatitis C: CMP, CBC today. Patient deferring treatment.
- IVDU in sustained remission.
Follow up 1 year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs back: no change from prior years. Liver enzymes mildly elevated as usual with normal liver function and platelets; kidneys and blood count normal.

documents.title: Immunizations

documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, 2025-26 COVID vaccine 0.3 mL IM R deltoid. Screening questions negative. No adverse reaction.

Reply (RN, 12/1, for PCP): Congratulations! Noted in your chart and the PCP is aware. Keep taking your prenatal vitamin. OB will follow you closely given the last pregnancies; reach out to us for anything outside of pregnancy care.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — LABOR & DELIVERY
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 07/28/2026   Discharge 08/01/2026
Principal diagnosis: Category III fetal heart rate tracing at 39w0d
Secondary: clinically suspected recurrent placental abruption, not seen on ultrasound; history of abruption with cesarean (2024), AFLP (2022), PPROM (2020); chronic hepatitis C; hepatitis B non-immune
Procedure: emergency repeat low transverse cesarean delivery 07/28/2026

History: 35-year-old G4P0303 with a prenatal course that had been uneventful, presenting overnight after an hour of sudden, severe abdominal pain with vaginal bleeding and a sense that the baby was moving less than usual.
Initial assessment: BP 120/75, HR 88, temperature 37.0 C (98.6 F). Uterus tender and hypertonic. Bedside ultrasound did not show an abruption. Continuous fetal monitoring: recurrent late decelerations with minimal variability and no accelerations over a 10-minute observation.
Intrauterine resuscitation was begun — oxygen by face mask, IV fluid bolus, left lateral positioning — without improvement in the tracing.

Course: proceeded to emergency repeat cesarean. Liveborn infant admitted to the NICU for observation. Mother's postoperative course uncomplicated; incision clean at discharge, ambulating, tolerating regular diet.

Tdap given 05/12/2026 at the OB office.

Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin daily; ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed; acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed. No opioids at discharge, by patient preference given her history.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: OB incision check 1-2 weeks, postpartum visit 6 weeks; primary care within 2 weeks.

documents.body: Transition call after discharge 8/1 (emergency repeat C-section 7/28 for fetal heart tracing at 39 wks). Summary received yesterday, in chart. Pt home, baby discharged from NICU 7/31. Incision without drainage, no fever, pain controlled with ibuprofen/Tylenol. Light-moderate bleeding. Appointment with PCP 8/11.

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S:
35 y/o, 2 weeks out from emergency repeat cesarean at 39 weeks (7/28). Came in with sudden abdominal pain, bleeding and decreased fetal movement; uterus hypertonic, US without visible abruption, Category III tracing that did not respond to resuscitation. Summary reviewed. Baby went to NICU briefly, home since 7/31 and doing well.

She is recovering faster than last time. Incision check with OB was fine. Taking ibuprofen once or twice a day. Bleeding light. No fever, leg swelling, chest pain or dyspnea. Bottle feeding.

Hep C: she brought it up herself. "I want this taken care of now." Not breastfeeding. Would like the referral sent again.

Meds: prenatal vitamin; ibuprofen/acetaminophen PRN from discharge. NKDA.

O:
Vitals reviewed. Comfortable. Sclerae anicteric. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, incision healing well without erythema or drainage. Calves nontender. Mood good.

A/P:
1. s/p emergency repeat cesarean — routine recovery. CMP, CBC today.
2. Chronic hepatitis C, untreated since 2015 — re-referred to hepatology today for DAA treatment. Last elastography 2019 (5.8 kPa). Will forward their pre-visit lab requests.
3. PHQ-9 3.
4. Follow up here in about 6 weeks (booked 9/22).

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs look good for two weeks after surgery — blood count normal, kidneys normal, and liver enzymes in the same mild range they have always been with hepatitis C. The hepatology referral went out Tuesday.

documents.title: Hepatology pre-visit request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hepatology intake nurse called: referral received. They ask for a quantitative HCV RNA before her new visit so they can submit for treatment approval at the visit. Order placed per PCP. Called pt, she will come to the lab Friday morning.

documents.title: Lab draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Venipuncture L AC, one attempt. HCV RNA quantitative sent to reference lab. Pt tolerated well.

Reply (MA, 8/25): Hi Caitlin, the hepatitis C test is a send-out and isn't back yet. We'll message you when it is, and hepatology will get a copy. Your follow-up here is still on for 9/22.
